question: In a child with an unimmunised tetanus-prone wound, Tetanus Immunoglobulin (TIG) is the preferred passive immunisation agent over equine antitoxin because TIG has a lower risk of anaphylaxis and a longer half-life.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. TIG (human tetanus immunoglobulin) is preferred over equine antitoxin because it avoids hypersensitivity reactions (no equine proteins), has a longer half-life, and provides more reliable passive immunity. Always use TIG when available; equine antitoxin is used only when TIG is unavailable and requires skin sensitivity testing first.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. TIG (human-derived tetanus immunoglobulin) is preferred over equine antitoxin for wound prophylaxis and treatment because: (1) no risk of serum sickness or anaphylaxis from equine proteins, (2) longer half-life (3–4 weeks vs ~2 weeks for equine), and (3) more predictable bioavailability. TIG is used both for wound prophylaxis in unimmunised/under-immunised patients and as part of treatment for active tetanus.
